blog__ai-search-cites-people-not-brands.q: Which sources do AI search engines cite most?
blog__ai-search-cites-people-not-brands.a: User-generated and community sources dominate. Aggregated studies of AI citations across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, Gemini and Claude put Reddit at the top by a wide margin, with YouTube, Wikipedia, LinkedIn and Forbes completing the leading group. Reddit alone accounts for roughly 46.7% of social citations on Perplexity and 21% on Google AI Overviews, according to 2026 citation-index research.

blog__ai-search-cites-people-not-brands.q: Why do brand pages get cited less often than forums and social posts?
blog__ai-search-cites-people-not-brands.a: Because an AI answer is assembled to look independent. A vendor's own page is the least independent source available on a question about that vendor's category, so it tends to be used for facts about the company rather than as evidence in a recommendation. Community threads and named practitioners carry the perceived independence that a brand page structurally cannot.

blog__ai-search-cites-people-not-brands.q: Should B2B companies post on Reddit to get cited by AI?
blog__ai-search-cites-people-not-brands.a: Not as a tactic in itself. Undisclosed brand participation in community threads is detectable, gets removed by moderators, and destroys the independence that made those sources citable in the first place. The durable version is to have identifiable practitioners with their own audiences discuss your product publicly under their own names.

blog__ai-search-cites-people-not-brands.q: Does creator-led distribution improve AI search visibility?
blog__ai-search-cites-people-not-brands.a: It is a plausible and increasingly common thesis, but it is not proven for any individual company. What is measured is that the source types creators publish into — LinkedIn posts, YouTube, community threads — are heavily represented in AI citations. Whether a specific sponsored post causes a specific citation is not something current tooling can attribute.

blog__ai-search-cites-people-not-brands.q: Do brand pages still matter for AI search?
blog__ai-search-cites-people-not-brands.a: Yes, for a different job. Owned pages are where a model retrieves concrete facts about you: what you charge, what you do, how you compare. They rarely win the recommendation, but they answer the follow-up question once your name has been surfaced by something else. Both layers are needed.

blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-price-inde.q: What is the median price of a sponsored LinkedIn post in 2026?
blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-price-inde.a: Across 300 sponsored-post bookings placed on the Naano marketplace between 14 June and 11 August 2026, the median price paid was €180 per post for a creator with 5,000–10,000 followers and €300 for a creator with 10,000–25,000 followers. Below 5,000 followers the median was €84 [Naano Index, n=300, June–August 2026].

blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-price-inde.q: Why are published influencer rate cards higher than what brands actually pay?
blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-price-inde.a: Rate cards are asking prices published by the creators and platforms that benefit from a high anchor; transacted prices are the outcome of a negotiation between a specific brand and a specific creator. On Naano's own marketplace, the median transacted price for a sub-10,000-follower creator was €111, while widely cited 2026 rate-card guides quote $500–$2,500 for the same tier. Neither number is dishonest — they measure different things, and only one of them is what leaves a bank account.

blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-price-inde.q: How much does follower count explain about a LinkedIn creator's price?
blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-price-inde.a: Roughly 29%. Regressing listed per-post price on follower count for the 769 creators open for bookings at the snapshot time gives an R-squared of 0.289 on a log-log fit — so about 71% of the variance is not explained by follower count in this one-variable model [Naano Index snapshot, n=769, 11 August 2026 at 19:05 UTC]. The figure has been stable across two snapshots on a growing base, which is the most reassuring consistency check in the series.

blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-price-inde.q: How wide is the price spread between creators with the same audience size?
blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-price-inde.a: Very wide. Among the 205 Naano creators with 10,000–25,000 followers who were open for bookings at the snapshot time, the 10th percentile asked €27 per post and the 90th percentile asked €612 — a 22.7x spread at an identical audience size [Naano Index snapshot, n=205, 11 August 2026 at 19:05 UTC]. Follower tier alone is not a pricing benchmark.

blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-price-inde.q: Do cheaper sponsored post bookings get delivered less often?
blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-price-inde.a: In Naano's data, yes, and by a wide margin, although the relationship is correlational rather than causal and the size of it is moving. Of the bookings that reached a final state, 64.6% of those priced at €600+ per post ended in a published post, versus 30.4% of those priced under €200. A related response pattern is also visible: 41.6% of sub-€200 offers expired without the creator answering, against 19.2% of €600+ offers [Naano Index snapshot, n=279 settled offers, 11 August 2026 at 19:05 UTC]. Eight days earlier the same query returned 80.6% and 8.1%, so treat the magnitude as provisional and the direction as robust.

blog__how-to-find-brand-deals-on-linkedi.q: How do you find brand deals on LinkedIn?
blog__how-to-find-brand-deals-on-linkedi.a: Start with products your audience already needs, identify the person responsible for creator, content or demand-generation programmes, and pitch one audience-native post angle rather than a generic media kit. Add a marketplace route if you want bookable opportunities without running all of the prospecting yourself.

blog__how-to-find-brand-deals-on-linkedi.q: How many followers do you need for LinkedIn brand deals?
blog__how-to-find-brand-deals-on-linkedi.a: There is no universal threshold. A B2B brand can value a small, concentrated audience of relevant practitioners more than a larger general audience. Show who reads and responds to your work, what subjects you cover consistently and how a sponsor fits that context.

blog__how-to-find-brand-deals-on-linkedi.q: Should a creator charge per click for a LinkedIn sponsored post?
blog__how-to-find-brand-deals-on-linkedi.a: A creator should price the work and rights they control: the agreed post, review scope, publication window and any amplification permission. Clicks depend on distribution, audience response and the destination, so they should be measured without turning them into a guaranteed billing unit. On Naano, each creator sets a fixed fee per sponsored post.

blog__how-to-find-brand-deals-on-linkedi.q: Do LinkedIn brand deals need to be disclosed?
blog__how-to-find-brand-deals-on-linkedi.a: Yes. LinkedIn says content shared in exchange for money, products, services or another benefit must be labelled as a brand partnership and the commercial relationship must be clear, conspicuous and transparent. Creators should also follow the laws that apply to them and the sponsor.

blog__launch-b2b-linkedin-creator-campai.q: Can a B2B team launch a LinkedIn creator campaign in 30 days?

blog__launch-b2b-linkedin-creator-campai.q: How many creators should a first campaign use?

blog__launch-b2b-linkedin-creator-campai.q: How should a sponsored LinkedIn post be priced on Naano?

blog__launch-b2b-linkedin-creator-campai.q: What should a first creator campaign measure?
blog__launch-b2b-linkedin-creator-campai.a: Choose one primary outcome before launch, keep a unique tracked link for every creator, and review audience-fit evidence, visits and downstream conversions together. Do not change the lead definition or attribution window after seeing results.

free-tools__linkedin-engagement-rate-cal.q: What is a good engagement rate on LinkedIn in 2026?
free-tools__linkedin-engagement-rate-cal.a: It depends on audience size. As a rule of thumb for B2B accounts: under 2,000 followers, 5-8% by followers is good; 2,000-5,000 followers, 4-6%; 5,000-20,000 followers, 2.5-4%; 20,000-50,000 followers, 1.5-2.5%; and above 50,000 followers, 1-1.5%. Rates above those ranges are excellent, and rates below them usually signal a content or consistency problem rather than an audience problem.

free-tools__linkedin-engagement-rate-cal.q: Should I measure engagement rate by followers or by impressions?
free-tools__linkedin-engagement-rate-cal.a: Use both. Engagement rate by followers ((reactions + comments + reposts) divided by followers) is the standard public metric because anyone can compute it. Engagement rate by impressions divides the same engagements by how many people actually saw the post, so it measures content quality independently of how often LinkedIn distributed it. By-impressions is the fairer metric; by-followers is the comparable one.

free-tools__linkedin-engagement-rate-cal.q: Why do micro-creators have higher engagement rates than large accounts?
free-tools__linkedin-engagement-rate-cal.a: Smaller audiences are denser: a 3,000-follower creator is mostly followed by people who know their niche and interact regularly, while a 100,000-follower account accumulates passive followers who rarely see or touch its posts. LinkedIn also distributes posts through active commenters' networks, which favors tight communities. This is why B2B sponsors increasingly prefer several micro-creators over one large account for the same budget.

free-tools__linkedin-engagement-rate-cal.q: How do sponsors use engagement rate to set flat-fee post rates?
free-tools__linkedin-engagement-rate-cal.a: On marketplaces like Naano, each creator sets a flat fee per sponsored post, starting from 100 euros. Sponsors compare that fee against the creator's engagement rate and audience fit: a creator with 4,000 followers and a 6% engagement rate reliably delivers more qualified attention per euro than a bigger account at 1%. A strong, documented engagement rate is the single best argument for setting a higher per-post rate.

blog__what-is-a-b2b-creator-marketplace.q: Who uses a B2B creator marketplace?
blog__what-is-a-b2b-creator-marketplace.a: On the demand side, B2B SaaS marketing and GTM teams buying qualified traffic; on the supply side, practitioners (sales leads, RevOps managers, developers) from about 1k to several hundred thousand LinkedIn followers who monetize their audience per post.

Weight pricing transparency and vetting highest — a flat fee per post you can see before booking (from €100/post on Naano) is the most predictable model for B2B budgets.

blog__how-to-choose-b2b-influencer-marke.a: A platform is self-serve infrastructure — you pick and brief creators while the platform handles matching, contracts, payment, and tracking. An agency is a done-for-you service billed as a monthly retainer (typically €3,000–€10,000+) on top of creator fees, and the creator relationships stay with the agency, not with you.

blog__how-to-choose-b2b-influencer-marke.a: Pricing you can only get 'on quote', a creator catalog dominated by Instagram and TikTok lifestyle profiles, no in-platform payment (you handle creator invoices yourself), no per-post attribution, and annual licences or minimum spends that force a five-figure commitment before the first post goes live.

blog__how-much-charge-sponsored-linkedin.a: Per-follower pricing is a poor fit for B2B, because a 3,000-follower audience of RevOps managers is worth more to a sponsor than 30,000 generalists. If you need a sanity check, B2B rates in 2026 work out to roughly €30–€50 per 1,000 followers for creators with above-benchmark engagement, but the honest method is to price the tier, the engagement rate, and the vertical together rather than the follower count alone.

blog__how-much-charge-sponsored-linkedin.a: Charge a flat fee per post. best-b2b-influencer-marketing-platforms-.a: On Naano, creators set a flat price per sponsored post and there is no monthly platform fee. The median post transacted at €117 for a creator under 10,000 followers, €312 at 10,000–25,000 followers and €600 at 25,000–50,000 followers [Naano Index, n=239, June–August 2026]. best-b2b-influencer-marketing-platforms-.q: Are Kolsquare, Skeepers, Upfluence, or Traackr good for B2B?
best-b2b-influencer-marketing-platforms-.a: They are strong platforms for consumer brands, but none of them is built around LinkedIn or B2B buying audiences: Kolsquare and Traackr focus on Instagram/TikTok/YouTube brand programs, Upfluence on e-commerce and affiliate revenue, and Skeepers on UGC and product reviews. For B2B lead generation on LinkedIn, a B2B-native marketplace like Naano is the better structural fit.

best-b2b-influencer-marketing-platforms-.q: Should I use an agency or a platform for B2B influencer marketing?
best-b2b-influencer-marketing-platforms-.a: Use a platform when you want speed, transparent per-post pricing, and in-house control; use an agency when you need strategy and hands-off execution and can afford a retainer. The platform route keeps the cost of a failed test to a single post's flat fee — a median of €117 under 10,000 followers [Naano Index, n=100, June–August 2026] — instead of a monthly retainer that bills whether the content lands or not.

best-b2b-influencer-marketing-platforms-.q: What is the difference between Naano and Favikon or Upfluence?
best-b2b-influencer-marketing-platforms-.a: Favikon is a creator research tool (rankings and audience data, no booking or payment) and Upfluence is an e-commerce influencer database with outreach and affiliate tooling. Naano is a transactional B2B marketplace: you book a vetted LinkedIn creator at their flat per-post price, the platform handles payment, and every post carries UTM-tracked links.

blog__linkedin-dwell-time-b2b-creators.q: Does LinkedIn use dwell time to rank posts?
blog__linkedin-dwell-time-b2b-creators.a: Yes. LinkedIn Engineering says its feed models use dwell time and skip behaviour as passive-consumption signals. They sit inside a multi-objective ranking system alongside clicks, likes, comments, shares, relevance and creator-side feedback; LinkedIn does not describe dwell time as the single ranking factor.

blog__linkedin-dwell-time-b2b-creators.q: Is 30 seconds the LinkedIn dwell-time threshold?
blog__linkedin-dwell-time-b2b-creators.a: No public universal threshold exists. LinkedIn's 2024 engineering write-up says a fixed threshold introduced bias across content types and could not adapt to changes in the feed, so its newer long-dwell modelling uses adaptive thresholds.

blog__linkedin-dwell-time-b2b-creators.q: Can creators see dwell time in LinkedIn analytics?
blog__linkedin-dwell-time-b2b-creators.a: LinkedIn does not expose a post-level dwell-time metric in standard creator analytics. Use the metrics you can observe—qualified comments, saves, clicks and downstream conversions—rather than trying to reverse-engineer a hidden timer.

blog__linkedin-dwell-time-b2b-creators.q: Does Naano charge brands for 30-second clicks?
blog__linkedin-dwell-time-b2b-creators.a: No. Naano charges a fixed fee per sponsored post, set by each creator and shown before booking. Tracked links help brands compare traffic and downstream outcomes, but the marketplace does not bill per click.

free-tools__linkedin-creator-worth-calcu.a: It is an estimate, not a quote. free-tools__linkedin-creator-worth-calcu.q: What makes a LinkedIn creator worth more?
free-tools__linkedin-creator-worth-calcu.a: Engagement quality beats follower count. A creator with 8,000 followers and a 5% engagement rate is typically worth more per post than one with 50,000 followers and 0.5%, because sponsors buy attention from a relevant audience. Rates also rise with niche (B2B SaaS and finance audiences carry a premium), comment depth, posting consistency, and how senior the audience is.

free-tools__linkedin-creator-worth-calcu.q: How do creators get paid on Naano?
free-tools__linkedin-creator-worth-calcu.a: Each creator sets a flat fee per sponsored post, starting from €100. Companies see that price up front, book the post, and the creator is paid the fee once the post is published. There is no bidding and no percentage-of-spend arrangement: the creator decides the rate, and this calculator helps pick a defensible one.

free-tools__linkedin-creator-worth-calcu.q: Can companies use this calculator to budget?

blog__b2b-creator-campaign-tracking-temp.q: What should a B2B creator campaign tracker contain?
blog__b2b-creator-campaign-tracking-temp.a: Keep one row per published post with a stable campaign ID, creator ID, booking cost, destination URL, tagged link, publication time, post URL, visits, conversions, pipeline value and a notes field. Separate observed numbers from interpretation so the sheet remains an auditable record rather than a weekly performance story.

blog__b2b-creator-campaign-tracking-temp.q: Which UTM parameters should a creator post use?
blog__b2b-creator-campaign-tracking-temp.a: Use a consistent lowercase convention for utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign, plus utm_content to distinguish the creator and post. Keep the creator's name out of public parameters when an internal stable ID will do, and store the human-readable mapping in the campaign tracker.

blog__b2b-creator-campaign-tracking-temp.q: Should creator marketing use last-click attribution?
blog__b2b-creator-campaign-tracking-temp.a: Last click is useful as one observation, but it should not be the only view for a B2B purchase. Preserve the first creator touch, the converting session and the CRM opportunity history separately. Report what each model can prove instead of blending them into one invented contribution score.

blog__b2b-creator-campaign-tracking-temp.q: How often should a creator campaign be reviewed?
blog__b2b-creator-campaign-tracking-temp.a: Check links and landing pages before publication, reconcile delivery within one business day, review traffic and conversion quality weekly, and review pipeline on the sales cycle that matches the product. Do not cancel a creator after an hour of reach data or declare ROI before opportunities have had time to progress.

blog__how-long-b2b-creator-campaign-take.q: How long does a B2B creator campaign take from booking to published post?
blog__how-long-b2b-creator-campaign-take.a: A median of 8.0 days, with a 90th percentile of 14.1 days. That is measured across the 89 Naano bookings created between 14 June and 11 August 2026 that reached a published post [Naano Index snapshot, n=89, 11 August 2026 at 19:05 UTC]. The figure covers only bookings that were actually delivered; it is a turnaround time, not a probability of delivery.

blog__how-long-b2b-creator-campaign-take.q: How quickly do LinkedIn creators accept a sponsored post offer?
blog__how-long-b2b-creator-campaign-take.a: Very quickly. The median time between a brand sending an offer and the creator accepting it was 35 minutes across the same 89 delivered bookings [Naano Index snapshot, n=89, 11 August 2026 at 19:05 UTC]. Acceptance is not the slow step in a creator campaign.

blog__how-long-b2b-creator-campaign-take.q: Where does the time actually go in a creator campaign?
blog__how-long-b2b-creator-campaign-take.a: Almost all of it sits after acceptance. The median booking-to-published time is 8.0 days and the median gap between acceptance and publication is 7.7 days [Naano Index snapshot, n=89, 11 August 2026 at 19:05 UTC]. These are two independent medians rather than an additive split, but the gap between them is small enough to make the point: drafting, approval and scheduling consume almost the whole calendar, not discovery or negotiation.

blog__how-long-b2b-creator-campaign-take.q: What is the biggest schedule risk in a B2B creator campaign?
blog__how-long-b2b-creator-campaign-take.a: Non-delivery, not lateness. Among bookings that reached a final state, 30.4% of those priced under €200 per post ended in a published post, against 64.6% of those priced at €600 or more [Naano Index snapshot, n=142 and n=52 created bookings, 11 August 2026 at 19:05 UTC]. This is an association in a young and visibly volatile dataset, not proof that price causes delivery: the €600+ rate was 80.6% in the 3 August snapshot and fell to 64.6% eight days later on 11 extra bookings.

blog__how-long-b2b-creator-campaign-take.q: How much do sponsored post prices move in negotiation?
blog__how-long-b2b-creator-campaign-take.a: By about a quarter almost everywhere, with one clear exception. Among offers that went through Naano's negotiation flow, the average agreed discount was 25.3% under €100, 25.7% in the €200–€399 band and 24.7% in the €400–€599 band — but 37.1% in the €100–€199 band [Naano Index snapshot, n=26, 18, 25 and 13 negotiated offers, 11 August 2026 at 19:05 UTC]. Bands with fewer than 10 negotiated offers are not published.

blog__linkedin-engagement-rate-benchmark.q: What is a good LinkedIn engagement rate in 2026?
blog__linkedin-engagement-rate-benchmark.a: A good LinkedIn engagement rate in 2026 is 4–8% by followers for creators under 5,000 followers, 2–5% for creators between 5,000 and 20,000, and anything above 2% for accounts over 50,000. Measured by impressions, 5%+ is solid at any size and 8%+ is top-decile in B2B.

blog__linkedin-engagement-rate-benchmark.q: How do you calculate your LinkedIn engagement rate?
blog__linkedin-engagement-rate-benchmark.a: There are two formulas. By followers: (reactions + comments + reshares) ÷ followers × 100, averaged over your last 10–20 posts. By impressions: (reactions + comments + reshares) ÷ impressions × 100. The impressions version is the fairer measure because LinkedIn reach regularly exceeds follower count for small accounts.

blog__linkedin-engagement-rate-benchmark.q: Why do engagement rates fall as follower count grows?
blog__linkedin-engagement-rate-benchmark.a: Because audience precision dilutes: an account that grows past its core vertical accumulates followers who are less aligned with each post's topic, LinkedIn shows each post to a smaller share of a large following, and parasocial distance grows — people comment on peers far more readily than on semi-famous accounts.

blog__linkedin-engagement-rate-benchmark.q: How do sponsors use engagement rate to choose LinkedIn creators?
blog__linkedin-engagement-rate-benchmark.a: B2B sponsors treat engagement rate as a proxy for audience trust and attention, usually weighting it above follower count. On a flat-fee marketplace like Naano, a creator's ER and audience-fit justify their per-post rate — a 3,000-follower creator with 6% ER routinely earns sponsorships that a 60,000-follower account with 0.8% ER does not.

free-tools.q: Are Naano's free tools really free?
free-tools.a: Yes. The free LinkedIn creator search costs nothing, requires no account and no payment method, and carries no obligation to book anything afterwards. You keep the shortlist whether or not you run a campaign with Naano.

free-tools.q: Do I have to run my campaign on Naano to use the tools?

blog__get-paid-for-linkedin-posts-creato.q: How many LinkedIn followers do you need to get paid for posts?
blog__get-paid-for-linkedin-posts-creato.a: Far fewer than most creators assume. B2B brands buy relevance, not reach — a creator with 2,000 followers who are all RevOps managers is more valuable to a sales-tech company than a generalist with 100,000. On Naano the active creator base is typically 1k–30k followers inside a defined vertical, and creators start earning at the low end of that range.

blog__get-paid-for-linkedin-posts-creato.q: How much does a sponsored LinkedIn post pay in B2B?
blog__get-paid-for-linkedin-posts-creato.a: Entry-level deals start around €20 per post. Established creators in scarce verticals — devtools, RevOps, fintech, HR-tech — command €400 to €1,500 per post. The price is driven by how specific your audience is and how hard you are to replace, not by follower count alone.

blog__get-paid-for-linkedin-posts-creato.q: Do I need to register a company to get paid for LinkedIn posts?
blog__get-paid-for-linkedin-posts-creato.a: Not on a platform that handles it for you. This is the single biggest blocker for B2B creators, because most of them are salaried employees who cannot issue an invoice. Naano pays creators directly via Stripe or bank transfer within 24 hours of the post going live, with no invoicing required.

blog__get-paid-for-linkedin-posts-creato.q: Where can I find paid LinkedIn post opportunities as a creator?
blog__get-paid-for-linkedin-posts-creato.a: Three routes, in ascending order of reliability: inbound DMs from brands (unpredictable and often underpaid), direct outreach to companies you already use (slow, but the highest-paying), and B2B creator marketplaces where brands post briefs and you pick the ones you want. Marketplaces are the only route that gives you recurring deal flow without doing sales yourself.

blog__get-paid-for-linkedin-posts-creato.q: Will sponsored posts hurt my LinkedIn reach?
blog__get-paid-for-linkedin-posts-creato.a: A disclosed sponsored post written in your own voice performs close to your organic baseline. What damages reach is copy-paste brand messaging and outbound-style links with no context. Keep the angle yours, disclose the partnership, and post about products you would mention anyway.

for__devtools.q: Do developer audiences accept sponsored posts?
for__devtools.a: Yes, when the post is written by a practitioner in their own voice about a real workflow. Naano briefs are one page — context, constraints, link — and creators draft in their own words, which is why devtools CTR holds up.

for__devtools.q: What does a devtools campaign cost?
for__devtools.a: Fixed pricing from €20/post. Q1 2026 median CPL was €19 across 47 devtools campaigns — slightly above the platform mean, offset by the highest click-to-demo conversion of any vertical.

for__devtools.q: Can technical accuracy be enforced in the brief?
for__devtools.a: The brief carries your constraints and proof points, and you review the draft before it publishes. Edits stay light to keep the post native, but factual corrections are always in scope.

blog__naano-vs-traackr.q: Is Traackr good for B2B SaaS?
blog__naano-vs-traackr.a: Traackr is built for enterprise consumer programs — its customer base is overwhelmingly beauty and consumer brands managing large multi-market influencer rosters. For B2B SaaS teams that need LinkedIn pipeline rather than global program governance, a transactional marketplace like Naano fits better and costs far less to start.

blog__naano-vs-traackr.q: What is the main difference between Naano and Traackr?
blog__naano-vs-traackr.a: Traackr is influencer relationship management software: measurement, budgets, and compliance for programs you run yourself. Naano is a transactional marketplace: you book a vetted B2B LinkedIn creator at a fixed price from €20 per post, and the platform handles payment and qualified-click tracking.

linkedin-creator-marketplace.q: Is there a LinkedIn creator marketplace available in Europe?
linkedin-creator-marketplace.a: Yes. LinkedIn's own Creator Marketplace (announced June 10, 2026) is an alpha limited to advertisers in the US and Canada, with English-language content only and no announced European date. Naano is a B2B LinkedIn creator marketplace that is live in Europe today, with 2,000+ vetted creators publishing in local languages.

linkedin-creator-marketplace.q: What is the difference between Naano and LinkedIn's Creator Marketplace?
linkedin-creator-marketplace.a: LinkedIn's Creator Marketplace is a creator discovery tool inside Campaign Manager: brands search opted-in creators, see native follower and engagement data, and contact them by email — payment, contracting, and tracking remain the brand's problem. Naano is an end-to-end marketplace: brands book vetted LinkedIn creators at a fixed price per post, and the platform handles briefing, publishing, payment, and per-post tracking. LinkedIn's product is also US/Canada-only alpha, while Naano operates in Europe today.

linkedin-creator-marketplace.q: How much does a sponsored LinkedIn post cost?
linkedin-creator-marketplace.a: Based on 239 real sponsored-post bookings on the Naano marketplace between June 14 and August 1, 2026, the median transacted price was €84 per post for creators under 5,000 followers, €180 at 5,000–10,000 followers, and €312 at 10,000–25,000 followers. On Naano, each creator sets a fixed price per post, shown before booking — there is no cost per click or per impression.

linkedin-creator-marketplace.q: Is Naano an influencer marketing platform?
linkedin-creator-marketplace.a: Yes — Naano is a LinkedIn influencer marketing platform, structured as a marketplace rather than a database: instead of exporting a list of profiles and running outreach yourself, you book a vetted LinkedIn creator at a fixed price per post and the platform handles matching, briefing, payment, and tracking. It is built exclusively for B2B brands on LinkedIn.

The fixed per-post fee is known before the post goes live, and the platform pays the creator after publication — creators never issue brand-by-brand invoices, which matters because most active B2B creators are salaried professionals. free-tools__creator-campaign-budget-plan.q: How many sponsored LinkedIn posts can I get for my budget?
free-tools__creator-campaign-budget-plan.a: Divide the budget by the transacted median for the audience size you are buying, then multiply by the historical delivery rate for that price band. On Naano, the transacted medians were €84 per post under 5,000 followers, €300 at 10,000–25,000, and €720 above 50,000, while settled delivery rates ranged from 25.9% to 64.6% depending on the band [Naano Index snapshot, n=300 bookings, 11 August 2026 at 19:05 UTC]. A €5,000 budget books 59 posts at €84 but historically produced around 18 published ones.

free-tools__creator-campaign-budget-plan.q: Why should I plan on published posts instead of booked posts?
free-tools__creator-campaign-budget-plan.a: Because the two differ by a factor of three to five. Of the bookings that reached a final state on Naano, 30.4% priced under €200 ended in a published post against 64.6% priced at €600 or more, and 41.6% of sub-€200 offers expired without the creator ever answering [Naano Index snapshot, n=300 created bookings, 11 August 2026 at 19:05 UTC]. A forecast built on posts booked has been systematically optimistic at the low end.

free-tools__creator-campaign-budget-plan.q: Is it cheaper per published post to book many small creators or a few large ones?
free-tools__creator-campaign-budget-plan.a: Many small creators, by a wide margin. On these historical rates the lowest band costs roughly €280 per published post, against roughly €1,100–€1,300 for both the mid-tier and concentrated allocations — the cheap band's weak delivery rate is more than offset by how many more posts the same budget buys. The two upper allocations land close enough to each other that which one comes out ahead depends on your exact budget, so the tool computes it rather than asserting it. This is an observed association across a nine-week dataset, not a rule, and it is the opposite of the usual advice — the tool reports it because it is what the data says, not because it is convenient.

free-tools__creator-campaign-budget-plan.q: How long should I allow between booking a creator and the post going live?
free-tools__creator-campaign-budget-plan.a: Plan on 14 days rather than 8. Delivered bookings took a median of 8.0 days from booking to published post, with a 90th percentile of 14.1 days, and the creator accepted the offer in a median of 35 minutes [Naano Index snapshot, n=89 delivered bookings, 11 August 2026 at 19:05 UTC]. Almost all the elapsed time sits after acceptance, in drafting and approval.

free-tools__creator-campaign-budget-plan.q: Does this planner assume that paying more causes a post to be delivered?
free-tools__creator-campaign-budget-plan.a: No. The delivery rates are correlations across a young and visibly volatile dataset — the €600+ rate moved from 80.6% to 64.6% between the 3 August and 11 August snapshots on 11 additional bookings. A brand paying €600 typically also has a real budget, a written brief and an internal owner who follows up, and any of those could be doing the work. The planner applies observed historical rates to a budget; it does not claim that raising a price changes an outcome.

free-tools__sponsored-post-delivery-odds.q: What are the odds a sponsored LinkedIn post offer actually gets published?
free-tools__sponsored-post-delivery-odds.a: Observed delivery rates vary by price band, but the relationship is correlational rather than causal. Across 300 sponsored-post bookings placed on the Naano marketplace between 14 June and 11 August 2026, 64.6% of settled bookings priced at €600 or more per post ended in a published post, against 30.4% of those priced under €200. The rate for the €200–€399 band was 25.9% and for €400–€599 it was 34.6% [Naano Index snapshot, 11 August 2026, n=300 created bookings]. These rates move: the €600+ band read 80.6% in the 3 August snapshot.

free-tools__sponsored-post-delivery-odds.q: Why do cheap sponsored post offers fail?
free-tools__sponsored-post-delivery-odds.a: The snapshot cannot establish why an individual offer fails. It does show that 41.6% of offers under €200 and 40.9% of offers between €200 and €399 expired without the creator responding, versus 19.2% of offers above €600. Price may be associated with brand readiness, brief quality, creator availability or other factors, so these rates are risk signals rather than causal estimates.

free-tools__sponsored-post-delivery-odds.q: What is the median price actually paid for a sponsored LinkedIn post?
free-tools__sponsored-post-delivery-odds.a: €84 per post for a creator under 5,000 followers, €180 for 5,000–10,000, €300 for 10,000–25,000, €588 for 25,000–50,000, and €720 above 50,000 followers. These are transacted prices, brand-side and excluding VAT, from bookings placed on Naano between June and August 2026 [Naano Index, n=300].

free-tools__sponsored-post-delivery-odds.q: Does paying more actually cause a post to be delivered?
free-tools__sponsored-post-delivery-odds.a: Not necessarily, and this tool does not claim it does. The relationship is a correlation across a young dataset: a brand paying €600 typically also has a real budget, a properly written brief, and an internal owner who follows up, and any of those could be doing the work. What is directly measurable is that low-priced offers are far more likely to go unanswered — and that part is a creator-side behaviour you can price around.

free-tools__sponsored-post-delivery-odds.q: Should I just offer the creator's listed rate?
free-tools__sponsored-post-delivery-odds.a: In most cases, yes, for a first booking. Follower tier is a weak guide — follower count explains under a third of the variance in what creators charge (log-log R-squared of 0.289 across 769 creators open for bookings at the snapshot time), and at 10,000–25,000 followers the spread between the cheapest and dearest tenth of creators was 22.7x. The creator's own published rate is a far better anchor than any tier benchmark, including this one.

for__hr-tech.q: What does an HR-tech creator campaign cost?
for__hr-tech.a: Fixed pricing from €20/post. Q1 2026 median CPL was €20 across 34 campaigns — slightly above the platform mean, reflecting thinner creator supply and a wider buying committee.
The pool is thinner than sales or RevOps but growing; most briefs match in one pass. Naano flags upfront when a niche brief (e.g. comp-specific) needs a wider matching window.

for__hr-tech.q: Do HR audiences convert on creator posts?
for__hr-tech.a: Yes — HR professionals are among the most active LinkedIn audiences, and a recommendation from a People Ops voice they follow carries more weight than an ad in a category with high software fatigue.

blog__sponsored-post-brief-to-published-.q: How long should a sponsored LinkedIn post take to publish after you accept it?
blog__sponsored-post-brief-to-published-.a: About a week and a half. On the Naano marketplace, the median gap between a creator accepting an offer and the post going live was 7.7 days, and the full booking-to-published median was 8.0 days with a 90th percentile of 14.1 days [Naano Index snapshot, n=89 delivered bookings, 11 August 2026 at 19:05 UTC]. If you are routinely past two weeks, the bottleneck is almost always an unbounded approval loop.

blog__sponsored-post-brief-to-published-.q: What should a creator ask a brand before drafting a sponsored post?
blog__sponsored-post-brief-to-published-.a: Five things: what the product does in one sentence, who the post is for, the single link and its tracking parameters, any claim you must not make, and whether there is a hard publication date. Asking all five in one message on day zero is the difference between one revision round and four.

blog__sponsored-post-brief-to-published-.q: How do you stop a sponsored post approval loop from dragging on?
blog__sponsored-post-brief-to-published-.a: Cap it in writing before you draft. State that the price covers one round of consolidated comments returned within 48 hours, and that further rounds or a rewritten angle are quoted separately. A cap set after the second round reads as a complaint; the same cap set before the first draft reads as a process.

blog__sponsored-post-brief-to-published-.q: Do you have to disclose a sponsored LinkedIn post?
blog__sponsored-post-brief-to-published-.a: Yes, and you should want to. Disclose the paid relationship visibly in the post itself, in plain language, near the top rather than buried after the fold. Beyond the legal requirement in most markets, disclosure is what makes the endorsement credible to a B2B audience that assumes undisclosed promotion is happening anyway.

blog__sponsored-post-brief-to-published-.q: What should a creator send a brand after the sponsored post goes live?
blog__sponsored-post-brief-to-published-.a: A short wrap-up within 48 hours: the live link, the engagement numbers as they stand, the substance of any comments worth knowing about, and one concrete suggestion for a next post. It takes ten minutes and it is the single most reliable way to turn a one-off booking into a repeat one.

for__revops.q: What does a RevOps creator campaign cost on Naano?
for__revops.a: Fixed per-post pricing from €20 (median creator ~€150/post). Q1 2026 RevOps campaigns delivered a €17 median cost per qualified click across 41 campaigns.

for__revops.q: Is the RevOps creator pool big enough?
for__revops.a: Yes for core RevOps briefs; niche sub-verticals (PLG ops, usage-based pricing) have scarcer supply and may take an extra matching pass. The 2,000+ creator network is vetted per vertical before campaigns launch.

for__revops.q: Why not just run LinkedIn Ads against RevOps titles?
for__revops.a: You can — and the two compound. But RevOps CPCs are among the most competitive on LinkedIn, while a creator post reaches the same operators through a trusted voice at a fixed, known cost per post.

blog__linkedin-thought-leader-ads-vs-cre.q: What are LinkedIn Thought Leader Ads?
blog__linkedin-thought-leader-ads-vs-cre.a: Thought Leader Ads (TLAs) are LinkedIn's format for boosting posts published from an individual member's profile — an executive, employee, or external creator who approves the promotion — instead of from a company page. The brand pays LinkedIn auction prices (CPC/CPM) to extend the post's reach beyond the individual's organic audience.

blog__linkedin-thought-leader-ads-vs-cre.q: How much do LinkedIn Thought Leader Ads cost in 2026?
blog__linkedin-thought-leader-ads-vs-cre.a: TLAs are bought through the standard LinkedIn Ads auction, so costs track Sponsored Content: roughly €15–25 per click and €40–80 CPM for B2B SaaS audiences in 2026. There is no flat fee — spend scales with impressions and competition for your targeting, on top of whatever you pay the individual for the underlying post.

blog__linkedin-thought-leader-ads-vs-cre.q: What is the difference between Thought Leader Ads and booking a creator post?
blog__linkedin-thought-leader-ads-vs-cre.a: A TLA is paid amplification of an existing personal post, priced per impression/click by LinkedIn's auction. A booked creator post is the content itself: a vetted creator writes and publishes an authentic post about your product for a flat fee — from €100/post on Naano — and distribution comes from their organic reach. TLAs buy reach; creator bookings buy trusted content plus the reach it earns.

blog__linkedin-thought-leader-ads-vs-cre.q: Should B2B companies use Thought Leader Ads or organic creator posts?
blog__linkedin-thought-leader-ads-vs-cre.a: Use both in sequence: book creator posts at a flat fee to generate authentic content and measure which posts resonate organically, then run Thought Leader Ads (with the creator's approval) on the proven winners to add targeted paid reach. Starting with TLAs alone fails because you still need a creator relationship and a post worth boosting first.

for__vertical-saas.q: Are there creators for my specific niche industry?
for__vertical-saas.a: Supply is checked before you commit: Naano verifies matching creators for your niche at brief time and tells you upfront if the pool is thin. Vertical SaaS briefs sometimes take a wider matching window than horizontal categories.

for__vertical-saas.q: Why is vertical SaaS CPL higher?
for__vertical-saas.a: Scarce creator supply raises per-post pricing — Q1 2026 median CPL was €21 across 28 campaigns, ~15% above the platform mean. The compensation is audience fit: near-total ICP overlap versus single-digit relevance on broad channels.

for__vertical-saas.q: Is a small niche audience worth a campaign?
for__vertical-saas.a: In vertical SaaS, yes: a creator with 2,000 followers who are all in your industry out-delivers a 100k generalist. The qualified-click math favors precision over reach — the same logic covered in our nano vs macro creators data.

blog__linkedin-creator-discount-trap.q: Should I lower my rate to win my first sponsored post?
blog__linkedin-creator-discount-trap.a: Lower the scope before lowering the rate. In Naano's historical marketplace data, 30.8% of settled bookings under €200 reached a published post versus 80.6% above €600 [Naano Index, n=114 and n=41, snapshot at 2026-08-03 21:10 UTC]. This is an association, not proof that price causes delivery. If a brand's budget is genuinely smaller, offer a smaller deliverable rather than the same work cheaper.

blog__linkedin-creator-discount-trap.q: What is a reasonable discount to accept on a sponsored post?
blog__linkedin-creator-discount-trap.a: Ten to fifteen percent, and only in exchange for something: multiple posts booked at once, a longer lead time, or a case study you can publish. On Naano, the average agreed discount in the €100–€199 band was 37% — deep discounts cluster at the bottom of the market, not the top, where above €600 per post only one booking in 41 was negotiated at all [Naano Index, June–August 2026].

blog__linkedin-creator-discount-trap.q: How do I know if my LinkedIn rate is too low?
blog__linkedin-creator-discount-trap.a: Compare yourself against creators in your niche, not only against creators with your follower count. Follower count explains 29.0% of the variance in listed B2B creator prices [Naano Index, n=719, snapshot at 2026-08-03 21:10 UTC], and at 10,000–25,000 followers the P90 listed price is 25.3 times the P10. If nobody has ever hesitated at your price, test a higher rate rather than assuming the current one is optimal.

blog__linkedin-creator-discount-trap.q: Why do brands ignore cheap offers instead of declining them?
blog__linkedin-creator-discount-trap.a: In Naano's data it is often the creator side that goes quiet: 34.9% of offers under €200 expired without the creator answering, against 8.1% above €600 [Naano Index, n=204 settled offers]. The data shows the pattern, but not why each creator failed to respond.

blog__linkedin-creator-discount-trap.q: Is it better to charge less and post more often?
blog__linkedin-creator-discount-trap.a: Not on LinkedIn. Volume dilutes the thing you are actually selling — the trust of an audience that expects most of your posts to be unsponsored. Two well-matched sponsored posts a month at your real rate earn more than six discounted ones and cost you far less audience goodwill.

for__product.q: Does creator content work for PLG products?
for__product.a: Especially well: a post showing a real workflow drives self-serve sign-ups directly, and Q1 2026 data shows creator clicks convert to product sign-up at rates comparable to warm referral traffic.

blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-usage-righ.q: What usage rights are normally included in a sponsored LinkedIn post?
blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-usage-righ.a: The safest baseline is one disclosed organic post on the creator's own LinkedIn profile for the agreed fixed fee. Reposting the copy elsewhere, editing it into new creative, using the creator's likeness or running paid amplification should be written as separate permissions with a clear channel, duration and scope.

blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-usage-righ.q: Does a brand need permission to run a creator post as a Thought Leader Ad?
blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-usage-righ.a: Yes. LinkedIn requires the advertiser to request the member's permission before sponsoring an organic post as a Thought Leader Ad. That platform approval does not replace the commercial agreement between creator and brand about duration, fee, territory, edits and other uses.

blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-usage-righ.q: How should a creator price usage rights?
blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-usage-righ.a: Price the rights from the actual scope instead of applying a universal multiplier: where the content will run, whether media spend is paid, how long the permission lasts, whether the brand can edit the work, whether exclusivity applies and whether the creator's name or likeness appears. If the scope is not written, do not quote it as an unlimited bundle.

blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-usage-righ.q: Do usage rights remove the need to disclose a paid relationship?
blog__linkedin-sponsored-post-usage-righ.a: No. Licensing and disclosure solve different problems. A creator still needs a clear, hard-to-miss disclosure for the paid relationship, and the brand should preserve that context when it republishes or amplifies the endorsement. Platform labels can support the disclosure but should not be treated as the entire compliance plan.
